title: Promised $500 but paid $66 for the drum recording
summary: MGM had promised Lee $500 for the drum recording but paid union scale of $66 for two sessions, and he refused to work further.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah, it worked. So after that, what happened -- now they had promised me -- which was a lot of money -- they promised me $500 to do the recording. Okay? That's where the rub was. We did this session, and that's when the scale was $33 for 3 hours. $33. And so I guess I got my check, and they paid me for two sessions; we did two sessions, you know -- $66, and I called up and I said, you know -- I said that I would do, I would put the drum thing on there for $500. I didn't get but $66.

And so he says, well, you know, you want to make a name for yourself around town -- he tried to con me, you know, and I was always kind of a word person, you know, if you break your word with me, I couldn't live with that. So I said, "Okay, we'll just see who's gonna teach Mickey what I was doing when you get ready to shoot." I says, "You won't find me." You know ...so he says, "No, no, you'll be all right -- you're a young man, and you just got a chance and everybody is really impressed with you, and you're gonna get a lot of work here."
I says, "I don't want any work -- if you promise me $500 and I get $66.
